messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Cross-region health flapping detected. service: inference-router, affected regions: us-east <-> us-west, symptom: frequent health-check flips causing route churn and elevated 502s (pct err 6.4%). Automatic fallback engaged to eu for ~15% of traffic. Alert rule: health_check_flip > 5/min.

oncall-erin: @here seeing paging. I'll take it. marking P0. Paging pagerbot to wake second line if needed. :phone:

eng-sre-alex: on it — pulling region health timelines and LB logs. first-pass: looks like probe TTL set to 5s in us-west; us-east probes still 10s. That mismatch can cause rapid failover.

eng-runtime-lee: quick context — we rolled a routing policy change ~12:10 UTC that inverted fallback order (eu before local fallback) as part of canary. I flagged it but it passed smoke. Could be interacting with the short probe TTL.

support-jordan: CX -> several customers on paid tiers reporting request spikes and transient 502s, one customer (acme-corp) opened a support ticket and is seeing degrade on their endpoint for ~3min windows.

oncall-erin: alex/lee, plan? If fallback is bouncing traffic eu <-> us-west <-> us-east it will induce additional cross-region lat and more errors. We should stop automatic fallback while we stabilise.

eng-sre-alex: agreed. Suggested mitigation sequence (short):
1) Temporarily disable cross-region fallback in routing service (hold traffic to primary region)
2) Increase health-check debounce (probe TTL) on us-west to match us-east
3) Drain a couple of suspect LB nodes in us-west for 5m and observe

eng-runtime-lee: can do (1) now. I'm patching routing policy to force region_preference = local for 10m. Command:

```bash
$ rkctl routing update inference-router --policy '{"fallback_order": ["local","regional","global"], "temp_hold": 600}'
```

eng-runtime-lee: patch applied, verifying...

incidents-bot: ROUTING UPDATE: routing.policy changed by eng-runtime-lee. New policy heat: temp_hold=600s, fallback_order=[local,regional,global].

eng-sre-alex: increasing probe debounce on us-west to 10s to match us-east. patch applied to health-check config: `probe_interval: 10s, failure_threshold: 3`

support-jordan: confirmed reduced customer errors from 6.4% -> 1.1% for affected endpoints in the last 90s. acme-corp updated ticket: "latency dropped, 502s gone for last 2 minutes"

product-sam: good triage. We'll need an incident note and comms to a handful of customers who saw errors. Sam/Triage email?

eng-runtime-lee: also found an unintended side-effect: the canary policy we deployed had eu listed as a higher-priority fallback for some model_variants (vv-small) which caused the global fallback to prefer eu. That amplified cross-region hop. I put that canary back to the previous variant fallback order.

eng-sre-alex: draining two LB nodes in us-west (lb-west-12, lb-west-13) to force healthy consolidation. command: `infractl lb drain --name lb-west-12,lb-west-13 --timeout 300s`

incidents-bot: DRAIN JOB STARTED by eng-sre-alex on lb-west-12, lb-west-13 (300s).

pagerbot: second-line notified: oncall-maya. If condition recovers, stand down after confirmation.

oncall-erin: handing off — I'm staying on thread for 15m then handing to oncall-maya for follow-up. Alex/Lee continue monitoring.

eng-sre-alex: telemetry looks stable: health flip rate down to 0.3/min, error pct steady at ~0.9%. Rolling average latency stable.

support-jordan: CS note drafted, will send targeted customer update + link to status page. Will include "temporary routing hold" and expected follow-up postmortem.

product-sam: please log the exact policy diff so we can include root cause. Lee/Alex, file small PR with the rollback + tests.

eng-runtime-lee: filed PR #4921 with revert of canary fallback ordering and an explicit unit test for fallback precedence.

eng-sre-alex: wrapping up — removing temporary hold in 5m if metrics remain stable, otherwise we keep hold and escalate.

oncall-erin: 10:21 UTC summary: mitigations applied: temporary local-only routing hold, probe debounce unified (10s), drained suspect LB nodes, rolled back canary fallback ordering. Customer impact: transient 502s for some customers (max 6.4% of requests), mostly recovered after mitigations. Next: postmortem + fix to prevent mismatch between probe TTLs and routing policy canaries. Assigning postmortem to eng-sre-alex and eng-runtime-lee, comms: support-jordan, product-sam.

pagerbot: INCIDENT: status=investigating -> mitigated. Duration so far 00:11:20.

oncall-erin: handing to oncall-maya for 4hr follow-up. oncall-maya please ack.

oncall-maya: acked. I'll own the post-incident checklist and make sure the PR lands tomorrow.

product-sam: add action: add test harness that simulates probe-rate mismatch + fallback orders during canary. prevent future live loops.

eng-runtime-lee: noted. will add to roadmap and link to PR.

support-jordan: ticket updates sent. I'll collect impacted account IDs for billing/offset review.

oncall-erin: thanks all. closing active pages. Will update this thread with postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
